findings.title: Unrelated change to LOW_STOCK_THRESHOLD (5 -> 3)
findings.detail: The change lowers the inventory low-stock threshold from 5 to 3 in src/inventory/stock.py. No part of the bulk-discount proposal, design, spec or tasks mentions this. It changes which stock quantities count as low (for example, 3 and 4 are no longer low). The stock tests still pass, which suggests they read the constant rather than pinning the value, so this behaviour change goes undetected.
findings.suggested_fix: Revert the change to src/inventory/stock.py, or propose it as its own change.

findings.title: Out-of-scope, untested new module src/pricing/receipt.py
findings.detail: A 77-line receipt formatter was added. The spec does not ask for it, and the gate report lists no tests for it. It also leaves out the new bulk discount: the discount line it prints is only subtotal - total.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove src/pricing/receipt.py from this change, or specify and test it in a separate change.

findings.title: Threshold counts units, but no scenario separates units from lines
findings.detail: Q-001 was answered 'units', and the code sums quantities. Both scenarios hold whether the code counts units or lines, so the answered decision is pinned only by the implementer's test, not by the spec. For example, a single line of quantity 10 qualifies under unit counting but not under line counting.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a cart holds a single line of 10 units at 2.50 each THEN `bulk_discount` returns 2.50.

findings.title: Half-cent rounding of the discount is not pinned
findings.detail: Both scenarios give an exact cent value. A subtotal such as 25.05 gives a 10 % share of 2.505, and half-up rounding versus banker's rounding would differ there. The code rounds half up.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a cart holds 9 units at 2.50 and 1 unit at 2.55 (subtotal 25.05) THEN `bulk_discount` returns 2.51.

findings.title: Interaction with an applied discount code is not specified
findings.detail: bulk_discount uses cart.subtotal(), so it ignores any discount code applied to the cart. Two reasonable implementations differ here: one bases the bulk discount on the pre-code subtotal, the other on the post-code amount.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a cart of 10 units at 2.50 each also has a percentage discount code applied THEN `bulk_discount` still returns 2.50, computed from the subtotal before the code.

riskiest_assumptions: Cart.subtotal() returns a Decimal equal to the sum of unit_price × quantity, so 10 × 2.50 gives 25.00 and the result quantizes to 2.50.
LineItem's positional constructor order is (sku, unit_price, quantity), so the test builds the carts the scenarios describe.
The gate report's 'passed' status for test_bulk_discount_threshold_counts_units reflects a real run against the committed head.
